neighbours.label: ' a' (sometimes 'in' / 'are') right after 'is / was / as' when a physics statement says what something physically is: 'matter is a wave', 'the universe existed as a soup of particles'
fire: Quantum theory tells us that a beam of light is a stream of photons.
Shortly after its birth the universe was a dense sea of radiation.
In string theory every particle is a tiny vibrating loop of energy.
Physicists describe the electron as a cloud of probability around the nucleus.
According to relativity, mass is a form of energy.
To an astronomer, a neutron star is a ball of matter denser than an atomic nucleus.
Sound travels through the air as a wave of pressure.
Before atoms formed, the cosmos was a plasma of protons and electrons.
quiet: My neighbour tells us that her son is a student of law.
Shortly after its opening the restaurant was a favourite of local families.
In our village every farmer is a member of the cooperative.
Critics describe the novel as a portrait of life in the suburbs.
According to the mayor, tourism is a source of jobs.
To a shepherd, a border collie is a dog worth more than a tractor.
News travels through the town as a rumour at first.
Before the factory closed, the town was a centre of the shoe trade.

notes: Card: ' a' x14 of the top 32, all in physics or cosmology statements of what a thing is. Probe: electron is a wave 0.72, cosmos as a plasma 0.66, 'my uncle is a plumber' 0.09, 'office existed as a mess' 0.12. The + pole takes ' a'/' the' after 'in/on' in everyday text.
